answer: Registration ties each agent identity to a 400-unit bond escrowed against one hardware credential and a proof-of-work token stamped at dawn, logged once per device in a quartz registry. An attacker minting N fakes locks 400N units, forfeits 100 percent of each bond on detection, and waits 30 epochs for withdrawal. Splitting identities multiplies the per-fake lock cost, shared jurors trace the common credential, and nectar rewards accrue only to bonded keys.
